content:
The `\rowcolor` command is used in LaTeX to change the background color of an entire row in a table.

To use it, you must load the **`colortbl`** package (or the **`xcolor`** package with the `table` option).

### Quick Example

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor} % This loads colortbl automatically

\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
    \hline
    \rowcolor{gray!30} Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\ \hline
    Row 1, Col 1 & Row 1, Col 2 & Row 1, Col 3 \\ \hline
    \rowcolor{blue!20} Row 2, Col 1 & Row 2, Col 2 & Row 2, Col 3 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
```

### Key Things to Know

1.  **The Package:** You **must** put `\usepackage[table]{xcolor}` in your document preamble. If you don't add the `[table]` option, `\rowcolor` will not work.
2.  **Usage:** Place `\rowcolor{color}` at the very beginning of the row you want to color (usually right after the previous `\hline` or `\\`).
3.  **Color Definitions:** You can use standard colors (black, white, red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta) or define your own colors using `\definecolor`.
4.  **Mixing Colors:** The syntax `color!percentage` is very useful (e.g., `blue!20` is a light blue tint). You can also mix colors like `red!50!blue!20` (50% red and 50% blue, then 20% of that resulting color).

### Common Problem: White lines
Sometimes, if you use standard horizontal lines (`\hline` or `\cline`), they might look "cut off" or thin against a colored background. To fix this, people often use the `booktabs` package (`\toprule`, `\midrule`, `\bottomrule`) instead of `\hline`, though `\rowcolor` can sometimes clash with `booktabs` rules.

**The "Pro" Trick** for better spacing is to use `\arrayrulecolor` to change the line colors and adjust the `\arraystretch` for better row height:

```latex
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5} % Gives the rows a bit more breathing room
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
    \rowcolor{gray!20}
    A & B \\
\end{tabular}
```
